issues.description: The problem statement explicitly asks for a "public class Course" (and the template declares Course as public), but the solution implementation declares Course without the public modifier (internal by default). This is a visibility mismatch between the specification/template and the provided solution. Students comparing the solution to the instructions may be confused about the intended access level for Course (whether it must be public) and why the solution differs. While this does not prevent building the package (Course is only used within the same module in the solution), it is an unintended structural inconsistency in the exercise materials.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the solution's Course declaration match the problem statement and template by adding the public modifier (i.e. change `class Course {` to `public class Course {`). Alternatively, if Course does not need to be public for the exercise, update the problem statement (and the template) to remove the explicit requirement for `public` to keep all materials consistent.
